office.title: Indiana School Board Member
office.summary: A school board is the elected or appointed governing body of a public school corporation, the legal unit that runs a local school district [1, 2]. The board hires and evaluates the superintendent, adopts policies, and approves the annual budget, while the superintendent and staff run schools day to day [3]. Most boards have five or seven members serving staggered four-year terms [3]. Starting in 2026, candidates may list a political party, run as independents, or list no affiliation on the ballot, and there is no primary for these seats [2, 4].

facts.label: Term
facts.value: 4 years, with elections staggered so part of the board is chosen every two years [3]

facts.label: Elected
facts.value: At the November general election (November 3, 2026, or November 2028 for some seats); depending on the local organization plan, members represent the whole school corporation (at large) or a district within it, and some boards are wholly or partly appointed [2]

facts.label: Ballot label
facts.value: Each candidate chooses a party label, 'Independent', or no affiliation, shown next to the name; no primary and no straight-ticket voting for these races [2, 4]

facts.label: Pay
facts.value: Set by board resolution: an annual amount of no more than 10% of the lowest starting teacher salary in the school corporation, plus a capped per diem [5]

duties: Hires, evaluates and can dismiss the superintendent, and approves the hiring and firing of principals, teachers and other staff recommended by the superintendent [1, 7, 3].
Adopts the annual budget, appropriates funds and oversees school finances [1, 3].

Decides whether to ask voters to approve an operating referendum (an extra property tax levy); the board adopts the resolution and the Department of Local Government Finance reviews the ballot language for compliance with state law [8].
Approves contracts, buys and sells property, and decides on construction, repair and demolition of school buildings [1].

Bargains with the teachers' union over salary, wages and wage-related benefits such as health insurance and retirement; state law excludes teacher evaluation procedures from those bargaining subjects [9].
Writes and updates policies and rules for schools, often in a policy handbook, including the student handbook [1, 3].
Buys curricular materials, provides them to students without charge, and runs programs such as student transportation and school lunch [1].

Must adopt a process for parents and residents to ask that library material be removed as obscene or harmful to minors, review requests at public meetings and keep a public catalog of library materials [10].
Hears written appeals of student expulsions, unless the board has voted not to hear them [11].
Must take official action openly; Indiana's Open Door Law says public agencies' official action is to be conducted openly so the people may be fully informed [12, 13].

A school board member must have lived in the school corporation (and, for a district seat, the district) for at least one year before the election, and a teacher or other employee of the school corporation may not serve on its board [2].

What the board does not control: the State Board of Education adopts statewide academic standards [14], the General Assembly sets the state school funding formula in the state budget [15], and voucher (Choice Scholarship) eligibility is set by state law [16].
recent_changes: 2025: Senate Enrolled Act 287 allowed school board candidates to declare a party affiliation; the Indiana School Boards Association opposed the change, and a supporter quoted by WNDU, a Noblesville school board member, said it adds transparency [17].

2026: Candidates choose a party, 'Independent' or no affiliation on their nominating petition, and that choice appears on the ballot; a candidate claiming the Democratic or Republican party must have voted in that party's primary in the two most recent primaries they voted in, or have certification from the county party chair, or can be challenged and removed from the ballot [2].

July 2026: Chalkbeat reported, citing Indiana School Boards Association data, that 524 of 1,044 candidates chose a party, about 72% of them Republicans [18]; the Indiana Election Division's 2026 guidance and the wording of the law differ on the primary-voting test, a question county election boards decide [19].

February 2026: Senate Enrolled Act 25 set the order of school board candidates on the ballot, grouped by party, with candidates who list no affiliation placed after the party and independent candidates [20].

2025: Senate Enrolled Act 1, a property tax law, limits how much operating revenue districts can raise through taxes and restricts school referendums to statewide general elections in even-numbered years [21, 22].
2025: The same law requires districts to share operating revenue with brick-and-mortar charter schools that enroll their students, statewide starting in 2028 [21, 22].
2025: The state budget opened Choice Scholarship vouchers to all Indiana families starting in June 2026 [16].
2026: The Indianapolis Public Education Corporation, rather than the Indianapolis Public Schools board, now certifies Indianapolis Public Schools referendum questions for the ballot [20].

2023: Senate Enrolled Act 391 changed the so-called $1 law so the Indiana Department of Education can order districts that lost at least 10% of enrollment over five years to close schools under 60% capacity and offer them to charter schools [23].
2023: House Enrolled Act 1447 required school districts to set up procedures for complaints that library material is obscene or harmful to minors [10].

race_context: Concord Community Schools is in Elkhart, Indiana. It has seven schools: Concord High School, Concord Junior High, Concord Intermediate and four elementary schools (East Side, Ox Bow, South Side and West Side). The superintendent is Dan Funston [24].
Federal (NCES) data show 5,212 students enrolled in 2024-25, down from 5,288 in 2023-24 and 5,348 in 2022-23 [25].

The board has five members. Each is elected to a four-year term and must live within the school corporation's boundaries. Current members: Jennifer Davis (president, term 2022-2026), Tim Yoder (vice president, 2025-2028), Tara Towner (secretary, 2022-2026), Mike Malooley (2022-2026) and Tim Koontz (2025-2028) [26].

How seats are elected: in 2022 three seats were filled from one pool of eight candidates. Candidates could live in any district, but no more than one could come from District 3 [27]. In 2024 two seats were on the ballot (Koontz, Yoder and Stacy McDowell ran, vote for not more than two) [28, 26].

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the three seats won in 2022, held by Davis, Towner and Malooley, all of whose terms end in 2026 [26, 27]. All three are on the ballot for 'Elkhart Concord School Board, District 1' and no one else is listed [6]. The state list says 'vote for 1'. If the race fills all three expiring seats, as in 2022, all three incumbents would win. Voters should check the county sample ballot for the number to vote for [6, 27].
The 2022 race was decided by a recount. Davis and Towner kept their seats. Malooley won the third seat by 55 votes over Stacy McDowell, replacing incumbent Jared Sponseller [27].

Operating referendum: in a Nov. 2, 2021 special election, voters narrowly rejected renewing Concord's operating referendum, 1,514 (51.29%) to 1,438 (48.71%). The renewal would have cut the rate from 40.5 to 32 cents per $100 of assessed value. Funston said referendum money made up 10% of the overall budget [29]. No later Concord referendum was found.

Facilities: in April 2025 the Elkhart Truth reported a multi-year renovation plan. Phase one covered Jake Field ($16.2 million), Ox Bow Elementary ($13.2 million) and South Side Elementary ($17.7 million), with high school cafeteria, classroom and activity-center work to follow. The article did not say how the work is funded [30].
In 2026 the board unanimously voted to rename the district office the George S. Dyer Education Center, after a longtime Concord educator and administrator [31].
No reporting was found on how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects Concord's budget.
No 2026 Concord candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of the race was found. Statements below come from the candidates' district board biographies and 2022 election coverage.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board president; first elected in 2014 and seeking a fourth term [32, 26, 6].
background: Corporate treasurer at Indiana Wood Products in Middlebury [32].
Parent of two Concord graduates. Has volunteered in classrooms and with SOAR, and is a past PTO president at Concord South Side Elementary [32].
Treasurer of the Well Foundation and a member of Tri Kappa [32].
First elected in November 2014 and took office in January 2015; now board president [32, 26].
Led the 2022 field after the recount with 2,264 votes [27].
path_to_ballot: Listed on the state candidate list as Nonpartisan [6].

items: Her district biography quotes her: "Our state legislature places a lot of financial constraints on local school boards" [32].
After winning in 2022, the Elkhart Truth reported that she looked forward to improving the quality of education "while also being fiscally responsible for taxpayers" [33].
Her biography quotes her: "All children should have an opportunity to reach their full learning potential in a safe and caring environment" [32].

on_incumbent: Is a current board member and serves as president [26].
In 2022 she said: "I work with hands down the best school board in Indiana," and "We have a lot of things we're working on and I'm just excited to be able to keep moving forward" [33].
gaps: No 2026 questionnaire, forum appearance, campaign website or finance filing was found.

candidates.summary: Incumbent, first elected in 2022 after a recount, seeking a second term [34, 27, 6].
background: Coordinates quality assurance and training for Elkhart County Court Services, including staff at the Juvenile Detention Center and Juvenile Probation [34].
Moved to Elkhart in 2014 to join the Elkhart County Sheriff's Department, and has spent more than 15 years in law enforcement and corrections [34].
Purdue University bachelor's degree in industrial management [34].
Parent of a child in the district; has worked as a camp counselor and coach [34].
First elected in November 2022 and took office in January 2023 [34]. After the recount he finished third with 1,105 votes, 55 ahead of Stacy McDowell [27].
path_to_ballot: Listed on the state candidate list as Nonpartisan [6].

items: His district biography says he believes student success depends on trust and shared goals among parents, teachers and administrators, and that education "is a community affair" [34].

on_incumbent: No public statements on the board's record were found.

His district biography lists his term as expiring in 2029, but the board roster shows 2022-2026, and he is on the 2026 ballot. The roster and ballot are treated as correct here.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board secretary; appointed in August 2022 and elected that November, seeking a second full term [35, 6].
background: Bookkeeper for West on Warren in Middlebury [35].

Parent of two children in the district. Was secretary of the South Side Elementary PTO and its president for two years, and has substituted in the front offices at Concord High School and Concord Intermediate [35].

Appointed in August 2022 to fill the rest of Kelly Barr's term after Barr moved out of the district, then elected in November 2022 [35]. Finished second in the 2022 race after the recount, with 1,677 votes [27].
path_to_ballot: Listed on the state candidate list as Nonpartisan [6].

items: After her 2022 win she told the Elkhart Truth she was excited about "the good we can do for our kids and our teachers" [33].
